image_description: A large radio telescope dish viewed from a low angle against a clear blue sky. The dish features a white mesh surface supported by a complex truss structure. A receiver cabin is suspended at the focal point by struts. The base includes a massive concrete pedestal and mechanical housing.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous parabolic dish antenna of colossal scale, dwarfing all surrounding structures.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dish dominates the frame and appears significantly larger than the trees in the background, consistent with a large-scale installation.
The rim of the dish forms a smooth elliptical projection, indicating a consistent parabolic curvature without visible warping or irregularities.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Massive installation spanning an area visible from great distances.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a close-up/medium shot; the full footprint of the installation is not visible to verify its span from a distance.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Receiver feed horn at focal point of dish.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A distinct receiver cabin/structure is clearly visible suspended above the center of the dish by support struts.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Alt-azimuth or equatorial mount for celestial tracking.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dish is mounted on a substantial pivot mechanism at the base, allowing for tilting (altitude) and likely rotation (azimuth), typical of such mounts.
The truss work connecting the dish to the central hub implies a rigid but rotatable assembly.
A thick, solid concrete pedestal is visible at the bottom center, supporting the entire apparatus.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Metal mesh or solid aluminum panel dish surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The surface clearly exhibits a grid/mesh pattern rather than being a solid sheet, which is a common design for radio telescopes.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Astronomical instrument for detecting radio-frequency emissions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The overall morphology matches the specific class definition of a radio telescope.
Inferred from the presence of the heavy-duty pivot and motor housing at the base.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific taxonomic classification and distinguish from similar satellite dishes or radar arrays.
To verify the 3D consistency of the truss work and ensure the receiver cabin is correctly positioned in space relative to the dish.
To check for edge bleeding or fusion artifacts where the thin struts meet the sky or the mesh pattern dissolves incorrectly.
To detect any subtle texture anomalies or lighting inconsistencies in the metal/concrete surfaces.

focus_areas: Structural integrity of the suspension struts holding the receiver.
Consistency of the mesh pattern across the curved surface.
Physical plausibility of the mounting base.
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the connection points of the struts holding the receiver cabin. AI generators often struggle with the precise geometry of these tension/compression members. Also, verify if the mesh pattern follows the perspective of the dish correctly or if it flattens/warps unnaturally.
